raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Run the tests/unit/v1 suite on a self-hosted KUNLUNXIN XPU runner inside the vendor container, one test file per subprocess (torch_xmlir inits CUDA at import, so pytest --forked is unusable). A blocklist keeps new tests running by default:
  - ignore.txt   whole files/dirs that hang or wholly fail
  - deselect.txt individual node ids that fail

Environment handling, all per-machine via Actions variables so the same workflow works on hosts with different networks and storage:
  - proxy (KLXPU_HTTP_PROXY/KLXPU_HTTPS_PROXY): unset means direct access.
  - Hugging Face (KLXPU_HF_ENDPOINT + HF_HUB_DISABLE_XET): route model downloads through a reachable mirror and force plain-HTTPS LFS, since the Xet CDN is unreachable behind a mirror and otherwise stalls.

Ignored files cover known KLX-stack limitations: BKCL/XCCL single-communicator hangs (autotp/moe/muon/zero/ulysses), Triton unsupported, torch.compile intercepted by torch_xmlir, and GDS unavailable.

+#!/bin/bash
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# DeepSpeed Team
+#
+# Run the tests/unit/v1 suite on the klxpu (KUNLUNXIN XPU) accelerator, one
+# test file per subprocess.
+#
+# Per-file (not `pytest --forked`): torch_xmlir inits CUDA at import, so a fork
+# per test hits "Cannot re-initialize CUDA in forked subprocess" for any test
+# that touches CUDA. A fresh process per file avoids that.
+#
+# Hangs: DS_UNITTEST_TIMEOUT bounds a hung DistributedTest (framework calls
+# pytest.exit, ending just this file); the outer `timeout -s KILL` backstops a
+# non-distributed or collection-time hang.
+#
+# Blocklist (not allowlist) so new v1 tests run by default:
+#   - ignore.txt    whole files/dirs to skip (--ignore)
+#   - deselect.txt  individual node ids to skip (--deselect); the leading
+#                   tests/ is stripped since pytest's rootdir is tests/.
+
+set -uo pipefail
+
+HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
+ROOT="$(git -C "$HERE" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || echo "$HERE/../../..")"
+cd "$ROOT"
+
+IGNORE_FILE="$HERE/ignore.txt"
+DESELECT_FILE="$HERE/deselect.txt"
+
+# Per-file wall-clock cap (outer) and per-test timeout (inner).
+PER_FILE_KILL="${KLXPU_PER_FILE_KILL:-900}"
+PER_TEST_TIMEOUT="${KLXPU_PER_TEST_TIMEOUT:-600}"
+# Framework-side hang bound; keep under PER_FILE_KILL.
+export DS_UNITTEST_TIMEOUT="${DS_UNITTEST_TIMEOUT:-600}"
+
+readarray -t IGNORES < <(grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*#|^[[:space:]]*$' "$IGNORE_FILE")
+# Deselect ids, normalized to rootdir-relative form (drop leading tests/).
+readarray -t DESELECTS < <(grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*#|^[[:space:]]*$' "$DESELECT_FILE" | sed -E 's#^tests/##')
+
+is_ignored() {
+    local f="$1" ig
+    for ig in "${IGNORES[@]}"; do
+        [[ "$f" == "$ig" || "$f" == "$ig"/* ]] && return 0
+    done
+    return 1
+}
+
+mapfile -t FILES < <(find tests/unit/v1 -name 'test_*.py' | sort)
+
+npass=0
+nfail=0
+nskip=0
+failed_files=()
+
+for f in "${FILES[@]}"; do
+    if is_ignored "$f"; then
+        echo "IGNORE    $f"
+        nskip=$((nskip + 1))
+        continue
+    fi
+    # Deselect ids belonging to this file.
+    frel="${f#tests/}"
+    ds=()
+    for d in "${DESELECTS[@]}"; do
+        [[ "$d" == "$frel::"* ]] && ds+=("--deselect=$d")
+    done
+    timeout -s KILL "$PER_FILE_KILL" python -m pytest "$f" \
+        -p no:randomly -q \
+        --timeout="$PER_TEST_TIMEOUT" --timeout-method=signal \
+        "${ds[@]}"

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Expose all mapped devices to 8-GPU tests**

The container maps `/dev/xpu0` through `/dev/xpu7`, but this job-wide mask makes KLXPU's inherited `torch.cuda.device_count()` return only four. `DistributedExec._launch_procs` (`tests/unit/common.py:273-277`) skips any test whose world size exceeds that count, so the non-blocklisted `TestAutoEPZero3ReplicaGroups8GPU` (`tests/unit/v1/moe/test_autoep_integration.py:253-256`) is silently skipped instead of validating 8-GPU expert placement. Expose all eight devices (or explicitly classify this test as unsupported) rather than losing this integration coverage.

@@ -0,0 +1,79 @@
+name: klxpu-triage
+
+# Auto-file an issue when a nightly (scheduled) klxpu v1 run has test failures,
+# following the nightly-triage.yml pattern: a cloud-hosted workflow_run job reads
+# the completed klxpu run's log and reports through ci/nightly_report.sh, which
+# labels the issue and comments on an existing open one instead of filing a
+# duplicate when the same regression recurs. Pure infra/setup failures (no
+# FAILED test files) are left untriaged.
+#
+# Only scheduled runs on the default branch are triaged; PR/push/dispatch
+# failures are interactive and need no issue. The self-hosted klxpu job keeps
+# contents:read only -- issue filing runs here, on a cloud runner.
+
+on:
+  workflow_run:
+    workflows: [klxpu]
+    types: [completed]
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+jobs:
+  report:
+    if: >-
+      github.event.workflow_run.event == 'schedule' &&
+      github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'failure' &&
+      github.event.workflow_run.head_branch == github.event.repository.default_branch
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 10
+    permissions:
+      contents: read
+      actions: read
+      issues: write
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout report script at the nightly SHA
+        uses: actions/checkout@v4
+        with:
+          # Same revision the nightly ran, so the reporter matches that run.
+          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
+          fetch-depth: 1
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Collect failing test files from the klxpu run log
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+          KLXPU_RUN_ID: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
+        run: |
+          # run-tests.sh ends with "FAILED: tests/unit/v1/....py" per failed file.
+          gh run view "$KLXPU_RUN_ID" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --log \
+            | grep -oE 'FAILED: tests/unit/v1/[^[:space:]]*\.py' \
+            | sed 's/^FAILED: //' | sort -u > failing-tests.txt || true
+          cat failing-tests.txt || true
+
+      - name: File or update the triage issue
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+          GITHUB_REPOSITORY: ${{ github.repository }}
+          KLXPU_RUN_URL: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.html_url }}
+          KLXPU_SHA: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
+        # SHA-free titles: a recurring regression is one tracked issue that
+        # collects a comment per night, not a new issue each time. Pure infra
+        # failures (no FAILED test files, e.g. a checkout/image-pull/job kill)
+        # are left untriaged -- only real test failures open an issue.
+        run: |
+          if [ ! -s failing-tests.txt ]; then
+            echo "No FAILED test files in the run log; treating as infra/setup failure, not filing an issue."
+            exit 0
+          fi
+          {
+            echo "The nightly klxpu v1 unit run at $KLXPU_SHA failed with test-file failures."
+            echo
+            echo "Failing files:"
+            sed 's/^/- /' failing-tests.txt
+            echo
+            echo "Run: $KLXPU_RUN_URL"
+          } > issue-body.txt
+          bash ci/nightly_report.sh \
+            "klxpu nightly regression: v1 unit suite failed" \
+            issue-body.txt "$KLXPU_RUN_URL"

+#!/bin/bash
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# DeepSpeed Team
+#
+# Run the tests/unit/v1 suite on the klxpu (KUNLUNXIN XPU) accelerator, one
+# test file per subprocess.
+#
+# Per-file (not `pytest --forked`): torch_xmlir inits CUDA at import, so a fork
+# per test hits "Cannot re-initialize CUDA in forked subprocess" for any test
+# that touches CUDA. A fresh process per file avoids that.
+#
+# Hangs: DS_UNITTEST_TIMEOUT bounds a hung DistributedTest (framework calls
+# pytest.exit, ending just this file); the outer `timeout -s KILL` backstops a
+# non-distributed or collection-time hang.
+#
+# Blocklist (not allowlist) so new v1 tests run by default:
+#   - ignore.txt    whole files/dirs to skip (--ignore)
+#   - deselect.txt  individual node ids to skip (--deselect); the leading
+#                   tests/ is stripped since pytest's rootdir is tests/.
+
+set -uo pipefail
+
+HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
+ROOT="$(git -C "$HERE" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || echo "$HERE/../../..")"
+cd "$ROOT"
+
+IGNORE_FILE="$HERE/ignore.txt"
+DESELECT_FILE="$HERE/deselect.txt"
+
+# Per-file wall-clock cap (outer) and per-test timeout (inner).
+PER_FILE_KILL="${KLXPU_PER_FILE_KILL:-900}"
+PER_TEST_TIMEOUT="${KLXPU_PER_TEST_TIMEOUT:-600}"
+# Framework-side hang bound; keep under PER_FILE_KILL.
+export DS_UNITTEST_TIMEOUT="${DS_UNITTEST_TIMEOUT:-600}"
+
+readarray -t IGNORES < <(grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*#|^[[:space:]]*$' "$IGNORE_FILE")
+# Deselect ids, normalized to rootdir-relative form (drop leading tests/).
+readarray -t DESELECTS < <(grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*#|^[[:space:]]*$' "$DESELECT_FILE" | sed -E 's#^tests/##')
+
+is_ignored() {
+    local f="$1" ig
+    for ig in "${IGNORES[@]}"; do
+        [[ "$f" == "$ig" || "$f" == "$ig"/* ]] && return 0
+    done
+    return 1
+}
+
+mapfile -t FILES < <(find tests/unit/v1 -name 'test_*.py' | sort)
+
+npass=0
+nfail=0
+nskip=0
+failed_files=()
+
+for f in "${FILES[@]}"; do
+    if is_ignored "$f"; then
+        echo "IGNORE    $f"
+        nskip=$((nskip + 1))
+        continue
+    fi
+    # Deselect ids belonging to this file.
+    frel="${f#tests/}"
+    ds=()
+    for d in "${DESELECTS[@]}"; do
+        [[ "$d" == "$frel::"* ]] && ds+=("--deselect=$d")
+    done
+    timeout -s KILL "$PER_FILE_KILL" python -m pytest "$f" \
+        -p no:randomly -q \
+        --timeout="$PER_TEST_TIMEOUT" --timeout-method=signal \
+        "${ds[@]}"
+    rc=$?
+    # 0 = passed, 5 = nothing collected (all skipped/deselected) -> both OK.
+    if [[ $rc -eq 0 || $rc -eq 5 ]]; then
+        echo "PASS      $f"
+        npass=$((npass + 1))
+    else
+        echo "FAIL(rc=$rc) $f"
+        nfail=$((nfail + 1))
+        failed_files+=("$f")
+    fi
+done
+
+echo "================= klxpu v1 summary ================="
+echo "passed files : $npass"
+echo "failed files : $nfail"
+echo "ignored files: $nskip"
+if ((nfail > 0)); then
+    printf 'FAILED: %s\n' "${failed_files[@]}"
+    exit 1
+fi

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Run the v1 tests marked sequential**

Whenever this script runs, pytest finds `tests/pytest.ini`, whose `addopts` supplies `-m "not sequential ..."`; `pytest --help` describes `-m` as “Only run tests matching given mark expression.” Since this is the only pytest invocation, cases such as `tests/unit/v1/zero/test_zero_user_backward.py:845` and `tests/unit/v1/nvme/test_aio.py:222` are always deselected, and an all-sequential file returns 5 and is reported as `PASS` below. Add a companion sequential pass (as the other accelerator workflows do) or override this marker filter so the advertised v1 suite actually covers these tests.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Expose all mapped devices to 8-GPU tests**

The container maps `/dev/xpu0` through `/dev/xpu7`, but this job-wide mask makes KLXPU's inherited `torch.cuda.device_count()` return only four. `DistributedExec._launch_procs` (`tests/unit/common.py:273-277`) skips any test whose world size exceeds that count, so the non-blocklisted `TestAutoEPZero3ReplicaGroups8GPU` (`tests/unit/v1/moe/test_autoep_integration.py:253-256`) is silently skipped instead of validating 8-GPU expert placement. Expose all eight devices (or explicitly classify this test as unsupported) rather than losing this integration coverage.

+        --device /dev/xpuctrl
+        --device /dev/xpu0 --device /dev/xpu1 --device /dev/xpu2 --device /dev/xpu3
+        --device /dev/xpu4 --device /dev/xpu5 --device /dev/xpu6 --device /dev/xpu7
+      volumes:
+        - ${{ vars.KLXPU_AIO_SCRATCH || '/tmp/klx_aio_scratch' }}:/aio_scratch
+      env:
+        http_proxy: ${{ vars.KLXPU_HTTP_PROXY }}
+        https_proxy: ${{ vars.KLXPU_HTTPS_PROXY }}
+
+    env:
+      CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES: "0,1,2,3"
+      TMPDIR: /aio_scratch
+      HF_HOME: /tmp/hf_home
+      HF_ENDPOINT: ${{ vars.KLXPU_HF_ENDPOINT }}
+      HF_HUB_DISABLE_XET: "1"
+
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+
+      - name: Resolve conda env
+        shell: bash
+        run: |
+          source /root/miniconda/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
+          conda_env="$(conda env list | awk '$1 != "base" && $1 !~ /^#/ && NF {print $1; exit}')"
+          test -n "$conda_env"
+          echo "Using conda env: $conda_env"
+          echo "CONDA_ENV=$conda_env" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
+
+      - name: Environment report
+        shell: bash
+        run: |
+          source /root/miniconda/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
+          conda activate "$CONDA_ENV"
+          xpu-smi || true
+          python --version
+          python -c "import torch, torch_xmlir; print('torch:', torch.__version__)"
+          python -c "import torch; print('device_count:', torch.cuda.device_count())"
+
+      - name: Install DeepSpeed (working tree)
+        shell: bash
+        run: |
+          source /root/miniconda/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
+          conda activate "$CONDA_ENV"
+          env -u http_proxy -u https_proxy pip install -U transformers
